text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate and latency observed in eu-west-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. 5xx-rate > 2% over 5m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/ingest/eu-west-1 (auto-attached)

Maria R.: I'm oncall. Acknowledge. Starting triage. Which subsystems are spiking? any customer-facing impact yet? :pager:

Sam P.: Hosted API proxy 503s and Dedicated pool healthcheck flapping. Seeing a pattern: control-plane calls to STS/iam are getting 5xx/429s. Could be AWS API throttling in eu-west-1. Logs here:

```
2026-04-12T11:02:34Z proxy-1 ERROR auth: sts.AssumeRole -> 503 ServiceUnavailable
2026-04-12T11:03:01Z pool-manager WARN scale: control-plane API error 429
```

Lee T.: Datadog metrics delayed ~3-5m so dashboards are laggy. I'm pulling raw logs from ELK. 503s start at ~11:01 UTC. Also seeing increased latency on control-plane -> inference node KV cache calls but that might be downstream symptom.

Ashley (AM): Support reports ~12 customers in EU experiencing generation failures (error 503/504). Tickets #8341-8348 aggregated in the support queue. Affected Dedicated pools: dp-eu-001, dp-eu-004. Hosted region eu-west-1 also impacted for new requests.

Maria R.: Immediate mitigation plan: (1) fail traffic to adjacent region for new requests where policy allows (eu-west-2), (2) put Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 into readonly/fallback mode so we avoid scale/creation ops that hit control-plane, (3) increase retries/backoff for STS calls, (4) contact AWS Health/Support and post status. Sam/Lee take lead on execution. Nate monitor customer impact and support comms.

Sam P.: Executing routing override to route new Hosted API requests from eu-west-1 -> eu-west-2 at the edge router for customers without region pinning. Command (control plane):

```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/force" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from_region":"eu-west-1","to_region":"eu-west-2","percent":100}'
```

Sam P.: Pushed rule, edge propagation in progress. Confirming majority of new requests now hitting eu-west-2.

Lee T.: Disabling autoscaler & pool-create operations in eu-west-1 to stop control-plane churn:

/runbook disable-autoscaler eu-west-1 --reason "STS throttling"

Lee T.: Done. Also switching Dedicated pools dp-eu-001 and dp-eu-004 to read-only mode (no new allocations).

incident-bot: Action recorded: routing-override, autoscaler-disabled, pools-readonly. Incident ticket: INC-2026-4823

Maria R.: I'll open AWS Health link and create a support case. Aaron/infra team please DM me if you have higher priority items. Ashley, please send interim comms to affected customers: short note + ETA unknown.

Ashley (AM): Drafting message now. Will include mitigation steps and advise we are routing to eu-west-2 where possible. :writing_hand:

Sam P.: Observability gap: Datadog was delayed; raw request logs show eu-west-1 -> STS/iam 503s and 429s. Example stacktrace snippet:

```
error: failed to fetch token: error from STS: 429 TooManyRequests
stack: control-plane/auth.go:223
```

Nate S.: Contacting AWS support. I've opened case 1234567890 with priority high. Including request IDs and sample timestamps.

Maria R.: Are there quick fallbacks for auth? We have cached session tokens for some service accounts; can we extend TTL and serve from cache for short window?

Lee T.: Yes. Implemented temporary TTL extension for service-account tokens for requests that can reuse existing session. Patch applied to auth cache: TTL += 15m where token_age < 1h.

Sam P.: For Dedicated control-plane calls that still fail, adding exponential backoff + jitter in the control-plane callers. Will monitor errors. Deploying a small change:

```
- attempts: 3
+ attempts: 6
+ backoff: exponential(200ms) with jitter
```

Sam P.: Change deployed to pool-manager and auth clients (hotfix). Observing reduced 429s from our side, but upstream 5xxs persist.

incident-bot: AWS Health Dashboard update: "We are investigating increased API error rates in eu-west-1 for STS and EC2 APIs" (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/eu-west-1/incident/9876). Timestamped 11:15 UTC.

Maria R.: Good. Keep routing override until AWS confirms service recovery. Support please set impacted customers to priority SLA and offer apol for errors.

Ashley (AM): Sent message to customers and opened priority tickets. Copy of message:

"We're aware of elevated errors and latency in our EU region (eu-west-1). We're routing new traffic to eu-west-2 where possible and applying mitigations. Our team is actively working with AWS. We'll update you as we have more info."

support-bot: Tickets updated: #8341-8348 set to status "investigating" and severity "high".

Nate S.: AWS replied to support case: "We are experiencing a regional control-plane API throttling issue; mitigation in progress. Expected update within 45-60 minutes." They requested request-ids and client timestamps (provided).

Lee T.: Observability note: Datadog logs will be backfilled; for now rely on ELK and local node logs. I pushed a short dashboard showing error counts from ELK.

Sam P.: Metrics after routing override: Hosted API error rate down ~70% for new requests as they land in eu-west-2. Dedicated pools with pinned region still see errors — we're contacting a few customers to confirm if they can accept cross-region failover.

Maria R.: Handoff: I'm going offline for 30m to eat, Sam you own incident until AWS says clear or Nate asks for follow-up. I'll be reachable on call if needed. Handing to Sam P. :hand_over:

Sam P.: Acknowledged. I'll keep the channel updated every 10m and escalate to eng-sre if any regression. Current status: routing override active, autoscaler disabled, auth cache TTL extended, AWS investigating.

--- 11:48 UTC update ---

incident-bot: ALARM: 5xx-rate dropping but not fully resolved. Current 5xx-rate 0.8% (target <0.2%).

Sam P.: Reducing routing to 80% -> eu-west-2 to allow some capacity testing in eu-west-1. If 5xx creeps back up we revert to 100%.

--- 12:30 UTC update ---

incident-bot: AWS Health: "Service has recovered in eu-west-1 for the affected APIs. We are continuing post-incident checks." (link)

Nate S.: I'm seeing error rates return to baseline in control-plane logs. Rolling back routing override and re-enabling autoscaler in eu-west-1 in a staged way.

Sam P.: Re-enabled autoscaler (staged) and removed routing override. Monitoring for 15m.

Lee T.: Datadog metrics slowly backfilled and dashboards show recovery. No abnormal traces in post-mortem short window.

Ashley (AM): Sent follow-up to affected customers summarizing impact and mitigations. Offer: credits where SLA breached. Support queue updated.

Maria R.: Back. Thanks Sam/Nate/Lee/Ashley. Incident seems mitigated. Closing on-call ownership back to rotation. Next steps: postmortem, include timeline, root cause (AWS control-plane API throttling), and recommendations: add better cross-region failover playbook for Dedicated, improve cached token strategy, update observability fallback docs. Assign action items to eng-sre and infra.

eng-sre-rotation: Recorded incident closure and task creation: PM-INC-2026-4823-POSTMORTEM. Owner: Nate S. ETA 3 business days.

Maria R.: Closing thread. :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone.
